newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Purchasing Managers index soars.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Purchasing Managers index soars.

text.p: The Purchasing Management Association of Chicago said Friday that its monthly index soared in August, indicating continued strength in the Midwestern manufacturing economy.

The regional business group said its index jumped to 60.0 in August from 51.2 in July as its members reported gains in production, new orders, order backlogs and employment. The index had languished in a relatively weak range between 51 and 53 for four months.
An index reading above 50 indicates an expanding manufacturing economy while a figure below 50 signals a slowing. The last time the index dipped below 50 was in March, when it stood at 47.3.
The jump in the seasonally adjusted index prompted Wall Street economists to raise their forecasts for nationwide manufacturing activity in August.

The report, along with another from the Commerce Department that showed new orders received by U.S. factories climbed strongly during July, knocked the inflation-sensitive U.S. Treasury market lower. The benchmark 30-year bond fell nearly a full point and its yield climbed to 7.12 percent from 7.04 percent Thursday.
The Chicago index is often viewed as a precursor to the national report released a day or two later.

The National Association of Purchasing Management will release its August index of manufacturing activity on Tuesday. Preliminary results of a Reuters survey point to a reading of 52.5 in the month compared to 50.2 in July.
The Chicago association said the production component of its seasonally adjusted index staged a "fantastic rebound," climbing to its highest level since last October.
It also said that order backlog registered a major swing as it jumped to its October 1994 level.
A two-month decline in employment reversed as that index approached neutral at 49.7, it added.
The group also said that prices its members' companies paid for raw materials also dipped, indicating that the "breadth of inflation shrinks."
The prices paid index fell to 51.8 in August from 53.0 in July. The employment component of the barometer rose to 49.7 in August from 43.2 in July.
